US-119-HR10918.title: Natural Gas Dominance Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10918.description: To amend the Clean Air Act to prohibit the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency from requiring the continuous monitoring of the net heating value or related parameters of certain combustion control devices, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10918.aiSummary: The bill would change the Clean Air Act rules for certain oil and gas sites. It would stop the Environmental Protection Agency from requiring some owners and operators to continuously monitor the net heating value, or related measures, of certain combustion control devices like flares. It would also set limits on how long some wells may send gas to a flare or control device during malfunctions or service breaks.

US-119-HR10819.title: United States-India Interparliamentary Group Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10819.description: To establish a United States-India Interparliamentary Group.
US-119-HR10819.aiSummary: The bill would direct the Secretary of State to seek an agreement with India within 180 days to create a U.S.-India interparliamentary group that would help both countries work on shared interests. If the agreement is reached, Congress would appoint up to 12 members to represent the United States, and the group would meet at least once a year with Indian lawmakers. It would also have to file an annual report on spending, and the bill would allow up to $100,000 a year for its costs.

US-119-S5658.title: A bill to prohibit the construction of data centers on Federal land, and for other purposes.

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5658.aiSummary: The bill would ban building data centers on federal land. It would apply to national forest land and land managed by the Interior Department, with some Indian land excluded from that definition. Any later transfer of federal land would have to include a rule that the land goes back to the United States if it is used for a data center, unless Congress specifically allows that use.

US-119-S5515.title: CARE for Moms Act
US-119-S5515.summary:
Community Access, Resources, and Empowerment for Moms Act or the CARE for Moms Act

This bill establishes and expands federal programs to increase access to health care for pregnant and postpartum women, particularly those in underserved communities. It also increases and expands excise taxes on tobacco products.

The bill requires state Medicaid programs and the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) to cover women for 12 months postpartum and to cover dental services for pregnant and postpartum women The bill also allows for two years of postpartum coverage for women under the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC).

Also, the bill establishes grant programs for
• state-based collaboratives to improve perinatal health care,
• mobile health units for obstetric care in rural and underserved communities,
• the doula workforce, and
• regional centers of excellence to educate health professionals on implicit bias and culturally competent care.

The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) must publish information on Medicaid and CHIP benefits for pregnant and postpartum women and report to Congress on maternal health needs and expenditures.

In addition, hospitals, as a condition of Medicare participation, must notify HHS at least 90 days before closing an obstetric unit.

Additionally, the bill increases existing excise taxes on cigarettes, equalizes tax rates among all other tobacco products, and establishes annual inflation adjustments. It also establishes new excise taxes for other tobacco products deemed as such by the Food and Drug Administration that are not already subject to such federal taxes.

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance. (text: CR S4998-5003)

US-119-S5515.aiSummary: The bill would expand federal health programs for pregnant and postpartum women, with a focus on underserved communities. It would require Medicaid and CHIP to cover women for 12 months after birth and to cover dental care during pregnancy and after birth, and it would allow two years of postpartum WIC coverage. It would also create grants for state groups, mobile obstetric care units, doula training, and centers that teach bias-aware and culturally aware care, while raising federal tobacco taxes.

US-119-HR2317.title: Northern Nevada Economic Development and Conservation Act of 2026
US-119-HR2317.summary:
Northern Nevada Economic Development and Conservation Act of 2025

This bill provides for the designation, conveyance, exchange, sale, or disposal of certain federal lands in Nevada.

Specifically, the bill provides for the transfer of ownership of federal lands from the Forest Service and the Bureau of Land Management to the State of Nevada, counties (Douglas, Clark, Pershing, and Elko Counties), cities (Carson City, City of Elko, the City of Fernley, and the City of Sparks), the Incline Village General Improvement District, and the Truckee River Flood Management Authority for economic development, recreation, or certain public purposes.

It also designates specified parcels of federal land as wilderness and as components of the National Wilderness Preservation System.

The bill also releases the reversionary interest of the United States in the Jean Prison site, thereby allowing the State of Nevada to use the land for purposes unrelated to the prison.

It also allows the Department of the Interior and the Forest Service to establish a federal complex for specified Bureau of Land Management, Forest Service, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Bureau of Reclamation, and Bureau of Indian Affairs offices or headquarters in Nevada on certain federal lands.

Additionally, the bill takes land into trust for the Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California.

US-119-S2787.description: A bill to amend the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 to ensure that ranchers who have grazing agreements on national grasslands are treated the same as permittees on other Federal land.
US-119-S2787.aiSummary: The bill would change a federal land law so ranchers with grazing agreements on national grasslands are treated the same as people who have grazing permits on other federal land. It would affect ranchers who graze livestock on national grasslands and the agencies that manage those lands. The measure was reported in the Senate with an amendment.

US-119-S4448.title: Accelerating Broadband Permits Act of 2026

actions.text: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. (text: CR S2173)
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S4448.description: A bill to require the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information to create tools for tracking the progress of grant recipients under the Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment Program, to require the Assistant Secretary to help executive agencies improve compliance with the statutory deadline for processing communications use applications, and for other purposes.
US-119-S4448.aiSummary: The bill would require the Commerce Department to make public tracking tools for broadband grant progress and for permit steps tied to those grants. It would also require help for federal agencies to track and report delays in processing communications use applications, with new data controls and alerts set within 90 days after enactment. The bill would also change a broadband project cost rule so a project with broadband infrastructure and a likely total investment of more than $5 million can count as a minimum-cost project under the FAST Act.

US-119-HJRES142.aiSummary: Signed into law, this resolution cancels a District of Columbia tax law and puts DC tax rules back in line with federal tax law. It restores several tax breaks, including a larger standard deduction, a $6,000 deduction for people 65 and older, and deductions for some tips, overtime pay, and car loan interest. It also affects DC changes to the child tax credit and some business tax write-offs.
